Topic1.Title: Annual Comprehensive Financial Report and Audit
Topic1.Summary: David Gross of the audit subcommittee explained how the city records transactions, prepares financial statements for its 45 funds, and has them audited by CliftonLarsonAllen. The auditors gave a clean opinion with no deficiencies, significant deficiencies, or material weaknesses. The city also received its 33rd consecutive Certificate of Achievement for Excellence in Financial Reporting. The audit committee unanimously recommended that Council accept the report, and council members thanked the committee and finance staff.

Topic2.Title: Open Comment Period
Topic2.Summary: Speakers pressed Council to raise the minimum wage by January 2024 rather than waiting until 2025. Union and labor leaders, immigrant workers, and Denver comparisons were cited, and the Boulder Chamber urged following the Consortium of Cities process. Others raised airport noise, the Marshall fire and Lahaina, the 0.15 sales tax split between arts and human services, and enforcement of the camping ban. Council asked staff for data on local wages and clarified that the 0.15 tax is not currently dedicated to a specific purpose and that the arts petition would go to the ballot unless withdrawn.

Topic3.Title: Consent Agenda
Topic3.Summary: Council pulled item 3J for separate discussion. One councilmember disclosed prior work with the property owners on the annexation item 3H and said they could remain impartial. Items 3A through 3I were approved unanimously on a roll call vote.

Topic4.Title: Ballot Measures for the 0.15 Sales Tax Extension
Topic4.Summary: Council took up second and third readings of ordinances for the November ballot. Ordinances 8586 (safe zones for kids) and 8587 (charter changes) passed unanimously. The 100% general fund option (8588) failed 5-4, and the 50/50 arts and general fund compromise (8591, with added language naming human services) passed 6-3 as an emergency ordinance. Staff explained the budget constraints and said the arts petitioners' conditional withdrawal takes effect with the compromise's passage.

Topic5.Title: Call-Up Check-In
Topic5.Summary: Council reviewed item 4A, a vacation of a 14-foot utility easement at 2950 Hawthorne Avenue. No councilmember expressed interest in calling it up.

Topic6.Title: Occupancy Limits: Staff Presentation and Council Questions
Topic6.Summary: Staff presented Ordinance 8585, which raises the limit on unrelated occupants to five citywide and changes the limit for two persons and their children to three. The ordinance also freezes occupancy at current levels for non-conforming uses, such as buildings with more units than the zoning allows. Staff summarized research, community engagement, and board recommendations (Housing Advisory Board and Planning Board 4-3). Council asked about affordability guarantees, code enforcement capacity, nuisance and parking tools, and the process that put the item on the work plan, which was a unanimous vote.

Topic7.Title: Occupancy Limits: Public Hearing
Topic7.Summary: More than 80 people signed up to speak. Most supporters were students, renters, co-op residents, housing advocates, and LGBTQ residents who said the limits are discriminatory and push people into illegal over-occupancy. Opponents, largely residents of the Hill and Martin Acres, cited the 2021 'bedrooms are for people' vote, noise, parking, trash, the lack of affordability guarantees, and the burden on university-adjacent neighborhoods. Some opponents asked for a ballot referendum or an overlay zone excluding areas near the university.

Topic8.Title: Occupancy Limits: Council Deliberation and Vote
Topic8.Summary: Rachel Friend moved to adopt Ordinance 8585. Lauren Folkerts' amendment to strike the non-conforming use and occupancy provisions failed 3-6. Supporters cited housing access, inclusion, sustainability, and legal stability for tenants. Opponents (Wallach, Weiner, Yates) raised concerns about the 2021 vote, the lack of affordability guarantees such as the ADU model, and neighborhood impacts. The ordinance passed 6-3 and the meeting adjourned at 11:13 pm.
